name: Docker Cloud Sandboxes

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go fixed sizes (micro..xl), per second
modes.note: Linear $0.07 per (1 vCPU + 2 GiB)-hour, metered per second while running (allocation, not utilisation). Stopped sandboxes (memory + filesystem preserved) pay no compute. TTL default 1 h, extendable to max 24 h from creation; default on-timeout = stop if resumable else delete. amd64 or arm64 'subject to account availability'.

plans.name: Docker Agentic Platform (pay-as-you-go)
plans.note: No recurring fee; billed monthly in arrears on a personal Docker account, separate from any Docker Personal/Pro/Team/Business subscription (which is not needed and not credited). Individual use only in the initial release: no shared workspaces or team ownership. Default quotas: 10 concurrent, 50 stored sandboxes, 100 volumes. Quota increases: process/price unpublished.

plans.name: AI Governance (org policy add-on)
plans.note: Organization-level sandbox policy governance, 'available on a separate paid subscription' (contact sales). Not a compute plan.

extras.price: BYO key, billed by your model provider (not by Docker; credits don't cover it)

extras.item: Local Docker Sandboxes (sbx on your laptop)
extras.price: Free, incl. commercial use; no Docker Desktop licence required

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Billed time per session vs useful time (sandboxes left to hit their TTL instead of being stopped)
knobs.why: Compute bills per second until the sandbox is stopped; the default TTL is 1 h, so an agent that finishes in 20 min but never stops keeps billing until expiry. Factor values are illustrative, not published.

caveats: Launched 2026-09-24; only one published rate card. Enterprise/volume pricing not published.
Default quota 10 concurrent sandboxes; higher concurrency process and cost unpublished (worked example of 50 concurrent needs a quota raise).
Hard cap 24 h from creation per sandbox (renew-timeout cannot go beyond); long jobs must be stopped/restarted or recreated.

Disk size per size tier not published (disk_gib null). Volumes are experimental and free; stopped-sandbox state storage free per 'Volumes, egress ... are free' and 'compute isn't billed while stopped'.
'Always-on' sandbox configuration appears in quota docs but has no separate price; assumed same per-second rate.

Standard one-time credit is $25 ($250 only for signups 2026-09-22..30). Credits expire 6 months after redemption; a valid credit card is required at signup. Credits cover sandbox compute only (setup, idle time and retries all count), not model-provider charges.
Isolation: product page says MicroVM; hypervisor unnamed. Region(s) unpublished (regions []).
Docker Pro/Team/Business subscription fees are separate and not needed; they do not include cloud sandbox credit.
All snapshots, including the one created when a sandbox is paused/stopped, are deleted after 7 days of non-use; stopped state is free but not durable storage.
Volume-backed sandboxes can't be stopped (TTL action must be delete); volume data is snapshotted only on exit, last writer wins.
Request rate limits exist and 'can vary by operation' but no numbers are published.

24 h cap is per lifecycle: resuming a stopped sandbox starts a fresh lifecycle timer; accounts with always-on access can use the 'restart' timeout action (stop+resume cycles preserving memory) and keep their concurrency slot while stopped.

fleet.tiers: Default 10 concurrent, 50 stored; per-account overrides may differ.
fleet.notes: Official API limits give default 10 concurrent, 50 stored sandboxes; stopped releases concurrency unless always-on, but retains stored count. Docs warn accounts can differ and instruct confirmation with Docker before capacity-dependent work. No explicit numeric higher tier or quota-increase procedure/turnaround found.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A cloud sandbox expires after one hour by default. On expiration, the service stops sandboxes that can be resumed and deletes the rest.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: TTL expiry (default 1 h, max 24 h from creation) with on-timeout 'stop' (the default for resumable sandboxes). Stop preserves memory AND filesystem ('Stop a cloud sandbox while preserving its memory and filesystem'; API: 'a backend advertising memory preservation hibernates it'), resumed on start/attach or automatically by an HTTP request to a published port (auto-resume lifecycle option). No idle-timeout trigger: the Console says a sandbox 'runs until you pause or delete it' or its timer expires. Always-on accounts get 'restart' = automatic stop/resume cycles preserving memory. Volume-backed sandboxes cannot be stopped (TTL action must be delete). Stopped-state snapshots are free but deleted after 7 days unused (per card).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Save a sandbox's state so you can start another sandbox from the same point later. A snapshot is separate from its source sandbox; restoring it creates a new sandbox with its own identity.
snapshot_on_demand.note: API CreateSnapshot 'checkpoints a running sandbox; a stopped source is rejected'. captureMode 'disk' or 'all' ('all captures memory and disk and requires memory-capture support'). RestoreSnapshot 'forks a new sandbox from a snapshot' (fork, source untouched). CLI equivalent: sbx --cloud template save <sandbox> <template> then create --template. CreateImage can also register disk content derived from a snapshot/sandbox as a reusable image.

harness_api.quote: To detach from an interactive run or attach session while leaving the agent running, press Ctrl+\. Reconnect with sbx --cloud attach <sandbox-name>. Reconnecting joins the existing agent session.
harness_api.note: Closest thing but not a harness API: sbx CLI / SDK kits launch Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Docker Agent, Gemini CLI, OpenCode (+Copilot, Droid, Kiro locally) inside the sandbox and you attach/detach to the agent's interactive terminal (TTY). No documented endpoint to send a prompt, stream structured agent events, send follow-ups or list/resume conversations; the API's process endpoints (CreateProcess / Interact / ReadOutput) are generic process I/O. Agents are preinstalled via kits (agent_harnesses = true).

egress_allowlist.quote: You can also match IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR ranges, such as 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.0/24, and 2001:db8::/32.
egress_allowlist.note: Account- and sandbox-scoped network policies (presets allow-all / balanced / deny-all; hostname patterns example.com, *.example.com, **.example.com, host:port; plus CIDRs). Deny wins over allow. Enforced by Docker's proxy outside the microVM ('All outbound TCP traffic passes through a proxy ... that enforces the network access policy'). CLI: sbx --cloud policy init deny-all; --allow-network / --deny-network at creation. API NetworkPolicy has allowNetworks/denyNetworks ('exact network names or CIDRs'). Policy decision logs available (sbx --cloud policy log).

egress_http_rules.quote: Cloud rules match network destinations. HTTP method and path restrictions, --protocol, and local governance profiles aren't supported.
egress_http_rules.note: Cloud only matches destinations. LOCAL Docker Sandboxes do support HTTP method + path rules ('A local policy rule can also match the HTTP method and path of a request'), so this may come to cloud later.

ingress_rules.quote: Treat an exposed URL as a public endpoint. Apply authentication in the service and remove the exposure when you no longer need it.
ingress_rules.note: Only control is choosing which ports to publish (sbx --cloud ports --publish/--unpublish; API CreatePort/DeletePort); nothing is exposed until you publish. Published URLs are public HTTPS, not protected by Docker account auth ('Docker account authentication does not protect the application URL'); no IP allowlists, tokens or private URLs; HTTP only, not a general TCP tunnel. SSH is via Docker-signed SSH certificates (IssueSSHCert), not a public port.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is a microVM 'with its own Linux kernel' and its own private Docker Engine; the agent 'runs as a non-root user with sudo privileges inside the VM' (security/isolation page). Docker Engine inside the VM itself programs iptables, so in-guest iptables/nftables should work. Not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Sandboxes using this secret receive a placeholder in PROJECT_API_TOKEN. The cloud proxy sets Authorization: Bearer <secret> on requests to api.example.com.
secret_proxy.note: Built-in services (anthropic, openai incl. OAuth, google, groq, mistral, nebius, xai, cursor, droid, github token) plus custom secrets for any exact DNS host (up to 10 hosts, chosen header + format, placeholder env var; wildcards and IP literals rejected). Account- or sandbox-scoped. HTTP header injection only; no database/SSH coverage documented (git over HTTPS to GitHub works via the github token). Caveat: credentials an agent writes to disk itself are captured in templates/snapshots.

volume_attach.quote: Keep project data after a sandbox is deleted by mounting a persistent volume. A volume is an independent resource: deleting a sandbox does not delete the volume.
volume_attach.note: Experimental, free, 100 volumes/account, must be enabled per account; attached only at creation. Not a live block device: 'Volume data is saved as a snapshot when a sandbox exits, not continuously.' Volume-backed sandboxes can't be stopped; memory-snapshot images don't support volumes.

volume_shared.quote: exclusive: exclusive permits one sandbox to attach the volume read-write.
volume_shared.note: API attachment mode is exclusive only ('it never silently enables shared writers'; cookbook: 'For Cloud Sandboxes, supply one entry and use exclusive attachment'). The CLI page does say concurrent mounts are possible but each sandbox works on its own copy: 'If multiple sandboxes mount the same volume at the same time, the last sandbox to exit overwrites the stored snapshot.' So no live shared filesystem; no read-only multi-attach mode documented.
